name: orbit-carousel

frames.best_why: Frame 1 shows the ring of eight avatars around a complete profile card with all its controls.

tagline: Profile photos orbit a ring while the chosen one fills a card in the centre.
summary: A team carousel where eight round avatars sit on a circle around a centred profile card. Stepping with the arrows, or clicking an avatar, swings the ring around with a springy overshoot and swaps the card.
appearance: A faint circle on black ringed by eight circular portraits, one edged in indigo. In the middle a small rounded card shows a larger photo overlapping its top edge, a bold name, a role and email in grey, and two chevrons either side of a purple Connect pill.
behaviour: Pressing an arrow or clicking a portrait rotates every avatar around the circle with a bouncy spring, and the card fades out and back in with the new person's details. The active portrait keeps its photo upright and carries an indigo ring.
demo_content: Eight teammates such as Maya Lin, Daniel Okafor and Priya Nair with roles like Product Designer and Staff Engineer.
search_phrases: team members arranged in a circle
click an avatar to see their info
use_when: A team or community page wants a memorable way to browse several people one at a time.
avoid_when: It uses fixed pixel sizes and a window-width check, so it does not really scale with its container.
customise: Pass a people array of name, role, email and photo; the ring radius, profile size and spring are fixed, and the Connect button does nothing unless you wire it.
weight_why: Eight avatars rotating with CSS transforms plus one card cross-fade.

a11y.note: Portraits are clickable images, not buttons, so they cannot be focused or opened from the keyboard; arrows work only globally.

issues: Frames 4 and 5 catch the card mid-swap, leaving it nearly invisible over the moving ring.
The Connect button has no click handler, so it does nothing.
polish_why: Springy orbit with a clear focus card; the dead Connect button and blurry swap frames are flaws.
